style: Read clearly and naturally, at a moderate pace
lines: Two saving plans, one race. Change either plan and watch who pulls ahead, and when.
The doubling penny starts with one cent. Watch day eleven, then look at what day thirty asks you to put in.
Here is the shortcut for a multiply plan. Write the sum, multiply it by the ratio, and subtract. Almost everything cancels.
Here is the shortcut for an add plan. Write the sum forward and backward, then add the two rows. Every column is the same.
Welcome to the Plan Desk. Each customer brings a goal, a deadline and a limit. Build a plan that works, or say it can't be done.
Ana needs three hundred dollars for a bike in twenty weeks, never more than twenty five dollars a week. Any plan is fine.
Ben adds one dollar more every week. He needs five hundred dollars in twenty six weeks. Pick his first deposit.
Cam's deposits grow ten percent every week. He needs four hundred dollars in twelve weeks. Pick his first deposit.
Dee starts with five dollars and adds the same raise every week. She needs four hundred dollars in sixteen weeks.
Eli wants to double every day for ten days and reach one hundred dollars, never more than sixty dollars in a day.
Fay's deposits shrink to eighty percent of the last one each week. She needs three hundred dollars in ten weeks.
Gus can start with five dollars at most and never go over forty five a week. He needs nine hundred fifty dollars in forty weeks.
Ivy needs two thousand dollars in twenty weeks. She can start with twenty dollars and never go over one hundred fifty a week.
That's the season. Look back at each plan, and at the one that could never work.
